filename: Stable Machine-Learning Parameterization of Subgrid Processes in a Comprehensive Atmospheric Model Learned From Embedded Convection-Permitting Simulations.pdf
title: Stable Machine-Learning Parameterization of Subgrid Processes in a Comprehensive Atmospheric Model Learned From Embedded Convection-Permitting Simulations
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: Subgrid atmospheric physics (convection, cloud microphysics, radiation, turbulence, convective momentum transport)
code_availability: ClimSim preprocessing and training code available at https://github.com/leap-stc/ClimSim. E3SM-MMF supporting pytorch-fortran coupling is available at https://github.com/NVlabs/E3SM. Simulation output data, saved models, and visualization notebooks are available at https://zenodo.org/records/12797810.
testbed_rationale: Uses the low-resolution ClimSim benchmark dataset and provides trained neural network weights and complete online coupling code via Pytorch-Fortran in E3SM, enabling standard multi-year offline and online evaluation.
pain_points: Online instability and rapid error growth when ML models extrapolate to out-of-distribution cloud states (e.g. unphysical liquid cloud near the tropopause and excess ice cloud in the stratosphere)
MLP models crash online within 1-3 months
Offline skill improvements do not necessarily translate to online stability without physical constraints
Persistent systematic online biases (tropical lower tropospheric drying and liquid cloud deficit, polar stratospheric temperature dipole)
Lack of model checkpoint restart capabilities due to tracking convective memory and large-scale forcing across previous timesteps
Coupled ML inference executed on CPU due to software engineering constraints rather than GPU, limiting run throughput
extraction_notes: The paper applies microphysical physical thermodynamic constraints (temperature-dependent liquid-ice partitioning and cloud removal above the tropopause level) to stabilize hybrid climate simulations for 5+ years.
